1:
Measure angles counter-clockwise from East. Bert starts at angle $0$ with angular speed $\frac{2\pi}{50}$; Ernie starts at $-\frac{\pi}{2}$ going clockwise at $\frac{2\pi}{60}$.

\textbf{(a)} They meet when their angles agree (mod $2\pi$):
\[\frac{2\pi}{50}t=-\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{2\pi}{60}t+2\pi k\ \Rightarrow\ 2\pi t\Big(\frac1{50}+\frac1{60}\Big)=2\pi k-\frac{\pi}{2}.\]
The first positive time is $k=1$: $t\cdot\frac{11}{300}=\frac34$, so $t=\frac{225}{11}\approx\boxed{20.45\ \text{s}}$.

\textbf{(b)} Bert does a lap (the circumference) in 50 s at 5 ft/s, so the circumference is 250 ft and $r=\frac{250}{2\pi}\approx39.79$ ft. In 100 s Ernie runs $\frac{100}{60}=1\frac23$ laps, so he is $\frac23$ of a lap ($\frac{4\pi}{3}$ rad) from his start. Straight-line distance (chord):
\[2r\sin\Big(\frac{2\pi}{3}\Big)=r\sqrt3\approx\boxed{68.9\ \text{ft}}.\]
2:
Write $H(x)=\dfrac{ax+b}{cx+1}$. $H(0)=21\Rightarrow b=21$. $H(1)=30\Rightarrow a+21=30(c+1)\Rightarrow a=30c+9$. $H(10)=55\Rightarrow 10a+21=55(10c+1)$:
\[300c+111=550c+55\Rightarrow c=0.224,\quad a=15.72.\]
So $H(x)=\dfrac{15.72x+21}{0.224x+1}$. As $x\to\infty$, $H(x)\to\dfrac{a}{c}=\dfrac{15.72}{0.224}\approx\boxed{70.2\ \text{inches}}$.
3:
\textbf{(a)} $V(x)=2b^x$ with $2b^{10}=5$, so $V(x)=2(2.5)^{x/10}$. Quadruple: $(2.5)^{x/10}=4\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{10\ln4}{\ln2.5}\approx\boxed{15.13\ \text{days}}$.

\textbf{(b)} At day 20: $V(20)=2(2.5)^2=12.5$. It drops linearly to $2.5$ at day 25: slope $\frac{2.5-12.5}{5}=-2$ dollars/day. Zero when $12.5-2(x-20)=0\Rightarrow x=\boxed{26.25\ \text{days}}$.

\textbf{(c)}
\[V(x)=\begin{cases}2(2.5)^{x/10}, & 0\le x\le20\\ 12.5-2(x-20)=52.5-2x, & 20<x\le26.25\end{cases}\]
4:
Put the buoy at the origin. Erik starts at $(-13,3)$, sails east at 8 mph for 0.75 h (6 miles) to $(-7,3)$, then sails south along $x=-7$.

\textbf{East leg} ($y=3$): inside when $x^2+9<100$, i.e. $|x|<\sqrt{91}\approx9.539$. He is inside from $x=-9.539$ to $x=-7$: $2.539$ miles, taking $\frac{2.539}{8}\approx0.317$ h.

\textbf{South leg} ($x=-7$): inside when $49+y^2<100$, i.e. $|y|<\sqrt{51}\approx7.141$. He goes from $y=3$ down to $y=-7.141$: $10.141$ miles, $\frac{10.141}{8}\approx1.268$ h.

Total time in the radar region: $0.317+1.268\approx\boxed{1.59\ \text{hours}}$.
6:
Put Juan at the origin. Sven starts at $(-60,0)$ heading toward $(45,80)$: direction $\langle105,80\rangle$, length $\sqrt{17425}\approx132.0$ m. At 3 m/s:
\[x(t)=-60+\frac{315}{\sqrt{17425}}t\approx-60+2.386t,\qquad y(t)=\frac{240}{\sqrt{17425}}t\approx1.818t.\]
\textbf{(a)}
\[d(t)=\sqrt{(-60+2.386t)^2+(1.818t)^2}=\sqrt{9t^2-286.36t+3600},\quad 0\le t\le44.0\]
(he reaches $(45,80)$ at $t=\frac{132.0}{3}\approx44.0$ s).

\textbf{(b)} $d=50$: $9t^2-286.36t+1100=0\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{286.36\pm\sqrt{42399}}{18}$, so \boxed{t\approx4.47\ \text{s}\ \text{and}\ t\approx27.35\ \text{s}}.
7:
Let $r$ be the circles' radius and $s$ the square's side. Wire: $2(2\pi r)+4s=100\Rightarrow s=25-\pi r$, with $0\le r\le\frac{25}{\pi}$. Area:
\[A(r)=2\pi r^2+(25-\pi r)^2=(2\pi+\pi^2)r^2-50\pi r+625,\]
an upward parabola.

\textbf{(a)} Minimum at the vertex: $r=\dfrac{50\pi}{2(2\pi+\pi^2)}=\dfrac{25}{2+\pi}\approx\boxed{4.86\ \text{in}}$ (area $\approx243.1$ in$^2$).

\textbf{(b)} The maximum is at an endpoint: $A(0)=625$, $A(25/\pi)=\frac{1250}{\pi}\approx397.9$. So the area is largest with \boxed{r=0} (no circles: all 100 in make one square, 625 in$^2$).
